Message.MsgText: The command did not complete successfully. See previous messages or error logs for details.

Explanation.p: One or more errors occurred during the execution of the command.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the previous messages displayed by the tdisrvctl command, or look at the error logs for more details.

Message.MsgText: Unknown value passed for '-op' option.

Explanation.p: An illegal operation parameter was passed.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the tdisrvctl command usage for allowed options.

Message.MsgText:
The server hostname does not support Tombstones.
Tombstone support is not available in pre-6.1 servers.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command tried obtaining Tombstones from a pre-6.1 server. Tombstone support has been introduced from v6.1 onward.

OperatorResponse.p: Connect to a version 6.1 or later server for viewing Tombstones.

Message.MsgText: Incorrect command usage.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked by passing unsupported command line options, or unexpected end of argument list was encountered or there was an incorrect usage of the command line options.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the tdisrvctl command usage and try invoking the tdisrvctl command with valid arguments.

Message.MsgText: Unable to get Tombstone manager.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was unable to connect to the Tombstone manager in the remote server. Probable reason being that the Tombstone feature was incorrectly configured on the server.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the remote server API and Tombstone manager settings on the remote server and try executing the tdisrvctl command again.

Message.MsgText: Only a single Config can be specified.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked by passing multiple Configs as a parameter to an option which allows only a single Config to be specified.

OperatorResponse.p: Invoke the tdisrvctl command by passing only a single Config at a time.

Message.MsgText: No value specified for option name option.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked by passing an option whose value had not been specified. The value is also required.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the tdisrvctl command usage, and invoke the tdisrvctl command again with the correct option and associated value.

Message.MsgText: Only a single AssemblyLine can be specified.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked by passing multiple AssemblyLines as a parameter to an option which allows only a single AssemblyLine to be specified.

OperatorResponse.p: Invoke the tdisrvctl command by passing only a single AssemblyLine at a time. Check the tdisrvctl command usage.

Message.MsgText: The value for the age option has to be an integer greater than zero (days).

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked by passing a non-integer or a negative value for the age (in days) option.

OperatorResponse.p: Invoke the tdisrvctl command by passing a valid integer (greater than 0) for the specified option of Tombstone.

Message.MsgText: Conflicting Tombstone option passed. Use keyword 'all' or specify a set of Tombstone attributes.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command with Tombstone option was invoked with contradictory options. Cannot ask for 'all' attributes and 'specific' attributes together.

OperatorResponse.p: Either specify the specific Tombstone attibutes that should be displayed, or ask to be shown all attributes. Not both. See tdisrvctl command usage.

Message.MsgText: The 'all' keyword should be the last argument passed.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command with Tombstone option was invoked with incorrect options. The 'all' keyword has to be the last argument passed.

OperatorResponse.p: See the tdisrvctl command usage.

Message.MsgText: The option switch option is mandatory.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked with a mandatory option not specified.

OperatorResponse.p: See the tdisrvctl command usage.

Message.MsgText: Could not locate Config Config name.

Explanation.p: Unable to locate the Config specified by user.

OperatorResponse.p: Check whether the Config name specified is correct and exists on the remote machine.

Message.MsgText: Connected to server hostname and port.
Config started: Config name
Config already running: Config name
Could not start Config: Config name

Explanation.p: Unable to start Config. An internal error occurred because the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server was not properly setup or the configuration was incorrect. This may also occur because the configuration file was password protected, and the user did not specify a password in the tdisrvctl command. Also, if the Config path is incorrect or not fully qualified, tdisrvctl will not be able to locate the Config.

OperatorResponse.p: See the tdisrvctl command error logs for help. Verify the configuration on remote server is properly set up. Additionally, verify the Config file is password protected. If so, then specify the password in the tdisrvctl start option using the -e switch. Also, ensure that the fully qualified path of the Config file is mentioned exactly as it appears on the remote machine.

Message.MsgText: AssemblyLine running: AssemblyLine name.
AssemblyLine started: AssemblyLine name.
AssemblyLine AssemblyLine name not found.

Explanation.p: Unable to find user specified AssemblyLine. The Assembly Name passed may be incorrect or misspelled.

OperatorResponse.p: Check whether the AssemblyLine specified exists in the configuration on the remote server.

Message.MsgText: Could not start AssemblyLines on the server hostname and port.

Explanation.p: Some exceptions occurred while starting the AssemblyLines.

OperatorResponse.p: Check whether the Configurations and AssemblyLines are correctly set up on the remote server. Also check the tdisrvctl error logs for more information on the errors.

Message.MsgText: The Config Config name is not loaded.

Explanation.p: The user specified stopping of components of a configuration which is already not loaded on the server.

OperatorResponse.p: Check whether the Configuration name is correct. Also check the tdisrvctl error logs for more information on the errors.

Message.MsgText: Config stopped: Config name.
Could not stop Config: Config name.

Explanation.p: Some exceptions occurred while stopping the configuration.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the tdisrvctl error logs for more information on the errors.

Message.MsgText: AssemblyLine stopped: AssemblyLine name.
Could not stop AssemblyLine: AssemblyLine name.

Explanation.p: Some exceptions occurred while stopping the AssemblyLine.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the tdisrvctl error logs for more information on the errors.

Message.MsgText: AssemblyLine already stopped: AssemblyLine name.

Explanation.p: The user specified AssemblyLine is already not running.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the tdisrvctl error logs for more information on the errors.

Message.MsgText: Error occurred while stopping AssemblyLines.

Explanation.p: Some exceptions occurred while stopping the AssemblyLines.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the tdisrvctl error logs for more information on the errors.

Message.MsgText: Cannot connect to server hostname and port.

Explanation.p: Unable to connect to server. This error might occur for one or more of the following reasons: If the server is not running, or the machine on which the server is running is not accessible, or the remote server API engine over RMI is not running, or if remote server API accepts only SSL connections, and the SSL parameters / certificates in the trust and key stores may be incorrect.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the tdisrvctl error logs for more information on the reason for connection errors. Try connecting again.

Message.MsgText: The server hostname and port has been shutdown.
Config Config name reloaded.
Config Config name is not running.

Explanation.p: The user tried reloading a Config that is not running / loaded. Only already loaded Configs can be reloaded. If the Config is not loaded, then start the Config instead of trying to reload it.

OperatorResponse.p: Give the tdisrvctl -op start command instead of reload command, or check the name of the Config.

Message.MsgText: One or more Configs could not be reloaded on the server hostname and port. Check the previous messages or error logs for details.

Explanation.p: There were some errors encountered while reloading Configs. One or more Configs failed to reload.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the tdisrvctl command error logs for details on the errors.

Message.MsgText: All the specified Configs have been successfully reloaded on the server hostname and port.
The operator switch option occurred more than once.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked with the same parameter passed more than once. Options can be passed only once. Fox example, the user may have passed the '-h' option twice, which is not allowed.

OperatorResponse.p: Pass each option only once.

Message.MsgText: Unknown option operator switch encountered.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked with an unknown option.

OperatorResponse.p: See the tdisrvctl command usage and invoke the command with the allowed options only.

Message.MsgText: The operator switch option was not specified. This is a mandatory option.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked without specifying the -op option.

OperatorResponse.p: See the tdisrvctl command usage and invoke the command with the correct and mandatory options specified.

Message.MsgText: It is mandatory to specify Config. 'all' keyword is not allowed with -c option.

Explanation.p: Instead of passing the Config name, the user asked for ALL Configs. This is not allowed. User must specify the configuration name.

OperatorResponse.p: Specify the explicit Config name when invoking the tdisrvctl command. See tdisrvctl command usage.

Message.MsgText:
Usage:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op operation [operation_specific_options]
general_options:
-h host remote server IP address or hostname(default is localhost)
-K keystore name of the SSL key database file
-p port port number(default is 1099)
-P key_pwd key file password
-s dir Specifies the working directory where the solution directory is located.
-T truststore name of the SSL trust store database file
-u userID username(for custom authentication)
-v run in verbose mode
-w user_pwd user password(for custom authentication)
-W trust_pwd trust file password
-? display command usage
operation:
event send custom notification event
prop manage Config properties
queryop query an AssemblyLine for operations
reload reload running Configs
report generate Config report or list Configs on remote server
shutdown shut down the server
srvinfo view IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server information
status view status of Configs or AssemblyLines
start start specific Config or AssemblyLines
stop stop specific Config or AssemblyLine
tombstone view Tombstone entries for specific Config or AssemblyLine
deletetombstone delete a tombstone entry
debug debug components in a running AssemblyLine
To get help for a specific operation:
tdisrvctl -op operation -?

The usage for reload operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op reload -c config_list
where:
-c config_list comma separated list of Configs to reload

The usage for shutdown operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op shutdown [-o return_code] [-f]
where:
-o return_code shutdown server with specified return code
-f force a controlled shutdown and exit all AssemblyLines

The usage for srvinfo operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op srvinfo

The usage for status operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op status [-c config_list | all]
[-r AL_list | all]
[-listen ]
where:
-c config_list comma separated list of Configs or keyword 'all'
-r AL_list comma separated list of ALs or keyword 'all'
-listen start receiving the logs of a running Config or AssemblyLine
Example:
To see the status of all loaded Configs and ALs
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op status
To see the status of all running ALs
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op status -r all
To see the status of all components of a particular loaded Config
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op status -c Config.xml -r all
Note:
- The keyword 'all' indicates all Configs or AssemblyLines.
- The -listen option requires exactly one Config or AssemblyLine to be specified.

The usage for the start operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op start -c config
[-e password]
[-r AL_list | all]
[-s ]
[-r AL_list -alop opname [{attr1:value1;attr2:value2;attrN:valueN}]|
-f filename]
[-m config_run_name -o storeName1=value1, storeName2=value2, storenameN=valueN]
[-t ]
[-listen ]
[-sync ]
where:
-c config name of config to start
-e password password of the config file if it is password protected
-r AL_list comma separated list of AssemblyLines to start or keyword 'all'
-s simulate mode run AssemblyLine in simulate mode
-alop opname AssemblyLine operation with required attributes and their values
-f filename filename to specify the operations
-m config run name run name of config
-o property file list comma separated list of property store names and values
-t start a temporary Config
-listen receive the logs of the specified Config or AssemblyLine
-sync execute AssemblyLine synchronously
Note:
- The -c option is mandatory.
- The keyword 'all' indicates all AssemblyLines.
- The -t option expects the Config specified in the -c option to be located on the client machine.
- The -listen option requires exactly one Config or AssemblyLine to be specified.
- The -listen option executes an AssemblyLine synchronously. There is no need to combine it with the -sync option. - The -sync option requires exactly one AssemblyLine to be specified.

The usage for stop operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op stop -c config
[-r AL_list | all]
[-f]
where:
-c config name of Config
-r AL_list comma separated list of ALs to stop or keyword 'all'
-f force a controlled shutdown of AssemblyLines
Note:
- The -c option is mandatory.
- The keyword 'all' indicates all AssemblyLines.

The usage for tombstone operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op tombstone -c config
[-r AL_name]
[-age n]
[[attribute_list] | all ]
where:
-age n display tombstone record for the last 'n' days
(default is 1 day)
-c config name of Config
-r AL_name name of Aseembly Line
all show all Tombstone attributes
attribute_list:
-ct component type
-cn component name
-cfg configuration name
-guid Tombstone entry's guid
-et event type
-ex exit code
-stime component's start time
-ctime Tombstone create time
-desc error description
-um user message
-stat statistics (valid for ALs only)
Example:
To see the last 2 days Tombstone entries (all attributes) for Config C1.xml
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op tombstone -c C1.xml -age 2 all
Note:
- The -c option is mandatory.
- Only one of the -r or -t option is allowed. Not both.
The Config Config name is not loaded on the server hostname and port.

Explanation.p: A Config that is not loaded on the server was specified for the 'report' option. Reports can only be generated if the specified Config is loaded on the server.

OperatorResponse.p: Check that the Config name specified is correct and that the Config is loaded on the server. Use the tdisrvctl 'status' option to obtain a list of the currently loaded Configs on the server. Alternatively, load the Config on the server and then fire the tdisrvctl command with the 'report' option.

Message.MsgText: The Config folder on server hostname and port is empty.

The usage for report operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op report [-c config | -l]
where:
-c config name of the Config whose report is to be generated
-l list the Configs in the remote server's Config folder
Note:
- The specified Config must be already loaded on the remote server.
- Only one of the -c or -l option is allowed. Not both.
The server hostname does not support 'config' folder. The 'config' folder support is not available in pre-6.1 servers.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command tried obtaining Config listing from a pre-6.1 server. 'config' folder support has been introduced from v6.1 onwards.

OperatorResponse.p: Connect to a v6.1 or later server for obtaining listing of Configs in the 'config' folder.

Message.MsgText:
The usage for event operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op event -e event_name [-s source]
[-d data]
where:
-e event_name name of the event to send
-s source the name of the source invoking the
event (default tdisrvctl)
-d data the data (message) to be passed to an
event listener (default is null)
Note:
- All events sent from tdisrvctl (-e option) are automatically prefixed by the string user.
Example:
To send an event user.process.X.completed from admin
tdisrvctl -h hostname -op event -e process.X.completed -s admin -d Admin triggered event.
The event event name successfully sent.

The usage for prop operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op prop -c config [-l] |
[ [-o store] [[-g key | all] | [-s key=value [-e]] | [-d key]] ]
where:
-c config name of the Config to use
-l list all the configured property stores
-o name of the property store to use
-g key get the value of the specified key (or keyword 'all'
implying get all keys)
-s key=value set the key to the specified value
-e encrypt the value when putting in the store (can
be used with -s option only)
-d key delete the specified key from the store
Note:
- The -c option is mandatory. The specified Config should be a loaded Config on the remote server.
- The -l, -g, -s, and -d options are mutually exclusive, and cannot be used together.
- The -e option can be used with only the -s option.
- The -o option is mandatory when using the -d option.
Examples:
To list all property stores for Config C1.xml
tdisrvctl -op prop -c C1.xml -l
To get all properties for Config C1.xml
tdisrvctl -op prop -c C1.xml -g all
To get all properties for Config C1.xml from store MyStore
tdisrvctl -op prop -c C1.xml -o MyStore -g all
To set a property MY_PROP to value MY_VALUE for Config C1.xml in store MyStore and mark it as protected
tdisrvctl -op prop -c C1.xml -o MyStore -s MY_PROP=MY_VALUE -e
Only one of the options -l, -g, -s, and -d can be specified. They cannot occur together.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked with options that are not allowed together. For example, the -l option is used for specifying the list of property stores, and hence cannot be used along with the -o option.

OperatorResponse.p: See the usage of the tdisrvctl prop option and invoke the command with the appropriate arguments passed.

Message.MsgText: The property store (-o option) is not specified.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command prop option was invoked without specifying the property store (-o option).

OperatorResponse.p: See the usage of the tdisrvctl prop option and invoke the command with the appropriate arguments passed.

Message.MsgText: Property store property store name does not exist.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command prop option was invoked with a property store name that does not exist (or was misspelled).

OperatorResponse.p: Fire the tdisrvctl command with prop option and -l switch to see the list of available property stores.

Message.MsgText: The property key property key does not exist.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command prop option was invoked with a property key name that does not exist (or was misspelled).

OperatorResponse.p: Check the property key name, or view all the available properties by using the -g option with the all keyword.

Message.MsgText: The server hostname does not support remote client event notification. This feature is not available in pre-6.1 servers.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was used to send an event notification to a pre-6.1 server. User event notification support has been introduced from v6.1 onwards.

OperatorResponse.p: Connect to a v6.1 or later server for sending remote client event notifications.

Message.MsgText: The server hostname does not support common APIs for IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator Property management. This feature is not available in pre-6.1 servers.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was used for property store management of a pre-6.1 server. Common APIs for IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator property store management were introduced from version 6.1 onwards.

OperatorResponse.p: Connect to a version 6.1 or later server for remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator property store management.

OperatorResponse.p: Refer the help for command, and pass appropriate command line parameters while invoking the command.

Message.MsgText: Parsing general options.
General Options: options.
Unable to determine server version. Cannot continue.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility was unable to determine the IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server version. It needs to know this to detect whether Tombstone Manager is present or not.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server version that you are connecting to using tdisrvctl. The tombstone support has been introduced in the IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator 6.0 version of the product.

Message.MsgText: Unable to obtain Tombstones.

Explanation.p: Some exception occured while trying to obtain tombstones. This could be because of some error in connecting to the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server, or because of some other error while communicating with the IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the error logs for other error messages, or try again.

Message.MsgText: Invalid age: age value.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked by passing a non-integer or a negative value for the age (in days) option.

OperatorResponse.p: Invoke the tdisrvctl command by passing a valid integer (greater than 0) for the specified option of Tombstone.

Message.MsgText: Error while processing shutdown return code.

Explanation.p: There was an error in converting the shutdown code into an integer value.

OperatorResponse.p: Ensure that the passed shutdown code is an integer value.

Message.MsgText: Unable to determine server version. Cannot continue.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility was unable to determine the server version, so as to detect if event notification APIs are supported in this particular server release or not.

OperatorResponse.p: Connect to a v6.1 or later server for sending remote client event notifications.

Message.MsgText: Error while trying to obtain list of property stores for Config: Config name.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility encountered an internal error while trying to obtain the list of configured property stores from the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server. This may have occured because the property store list in the remote server has got corrupted, or maybe an incompatible version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server is being used.

OperatorResponse.p: Check if the property stores list can be correctly seen in the ibmditk. Also, check the Problem Determination Guide for problems related to the property store. Ensure that the version of tdisrvctl and the version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server match. The property store feature has been introduced in version 6.1 of IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator.

Message.MsgText: Error while trying to obtain list of property stores for Config: Config name.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility encountered an internal error while trying to obtain the list of configured property stores from the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server. This may have occured because the property store list in the remote server has got corrupted, or maybe an incompatible version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server is being used.

OperatorResponse.p: Check if the property stores list can be correctly seen in the ibmditk. Also, check the Problem Determination Guide for problems related to the property store. Ensure that the version of tdisrvctl and the version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server match. The property store feature has been introduced in version 6.1 of IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator.

Message.MsgText: Error while trying to obtain property for Config:Config name.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility encountered an internal error while trying to obtain the properties of a particular store from the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server. This may have occured because the property store list in the remote server has got corrupted, or maybe an incompatible version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server is being used.

OperatorResponse.p: Check if the property values can be correctly seen in the ibmditk. Also, check the Problem Determination Guide for problems related to the property store. Ensure that the version of tdisrvctl and the version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server match. The property store feature has been introduced in version 6.1 of IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator. Also have a look at the output messages of the tdisrvctl command.

Message.MsgText: Error while trying to set property for Config:Config name.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility encountered an internal error while trying to set a property in a particular store in the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server. This may have occured because the property store in the remote server has got corrupted, or maybe an incompatible version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server is being used.

OperatorResponse.p: Check if the property values can be correctly set in the ibmditk. Also, check the Problem Determination Guide for problems related to the property store. Ensure that the version of tdisrvctl and the version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server match. The property store feature has been introduced in version 6.1 of IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator. Also have a look at the output messages of the tdisrvctl command. Try again.

Message.MsgText: Error while trying to delete property ''key name'' for Config:Config name

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility encountered an internal error while trying to delete a property in a particular store in the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server. This may have occured because the property store in the remote server has got corrupted, or maybe an incompatible version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server is being used. This would also happen in-case the particular property store is READ-ONLY.

OperatorResponse.p: Check if the property values can be correctly set in the ibmditk. Also, check the Problem Determination Guide for problems related to the property store. Ensure that the version of tdisrvctl and the version of the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server match. The property store feature has been introduced in version 6.1 of IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator. Also have a look at the output messages of the tdisrvctl command. Ensure that the particular property store is not READ-ONLY. Try again.

Message.MsgText: The KEY=VALUE format should have been specified for property key and value

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked incorrectly.

OperatorResponse.p: See the command usage and try again. Very double quotes are used to group arguments that have spaces.

Message.MsgText: Unable to retrieve server information.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility encontered an internal error while trying to obtain the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server host details.

OperatorResponse.p: Ensure that the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server is of version 6.0 or above. Also ensure that there are no connection errors while connecting to IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server, and the IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server has its remote server API engine is turned on.

Message.MsgText: Error while sending custom event notification: event name=event name, event source=event source, event data=event data.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility encountered an error while trying to send a custom notification event.

OperatorResponse.p: Have a look at the log trace, or the server logs to find out the problem. Ability to send custom notification was added in IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator version 6.1. Ensure that you are using a compatible version of IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server. Try sending the event again.

Message.MsgText: Unable to get the Config info or stop the Config.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility was unable to obtain handle to the remote Config to stop.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the exception, or previous messages. Also have a look at the server logs. Try again.

Message.MsgText: Unable to get details for AssemblyLines.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility was unable to get details for AssemblyLines. This may happen because the IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server version does not match the tdisrvctl utility version, or some other internal server error occured. The AssemblyLine or the Config could also be corrupted.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the exception trace, or the command output. Also check the server logs. Try again.

Message.MsgText: Unable to get list of all running Configs.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility encountered an error while trying to obtain the list of all running configs. This may happen because the IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server version does not match the tdisrvctl utility version, or some other internal server error occured.

OperatorResponse.p: Ensure that the tdisrvctl and remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server versions match. Also look into the exception trace and the server logs. Try again.

Message.MsgText: Unable to get list of all Configs.

Explanation.p: An internal error occured while trying to obtain the list of all configs. This occurred because of m_Session.listAllConfigurations() method threw an error.

OperatorResponse.p: Ensure that the tdisrvctl and remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server versions match. Also look into the exception trace and the server logs. Try again.

Message.MsgText: Error while getting assembly line details.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility was unable to get details for AssemblyLines. This may happen because the IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server version does not match the tdisrvctl utility version, or some other internal server error occured. The AssemblyLine or the Config could also be corrupted.

OperatorResponse.p: Check the exception trace, or the command output. Also check the server logs. Try again.

Message.MsgText: Error while getting Connector library details.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl utility was unable to determine the server version, so as to detect if config folder feature is supported in this particular server release or not.

OperatorResponse.p: Connect to a v6.1 or later server for viewing configs in the config folder.

Message.MsgText: Unable to get list of all Configs.

Explanation.p: An internal error occured while trying to obtain the list of all configs. This occurred because of Session.listAllConfigurations() method threw an error.

OperatorResponse.p: Ensure that the tdisrvctl and remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server versions match. Also look into the exception trace and the server logs. Try again.

Message.MsgText: Error while retrieving list of loaded Configs.

Explanation.p: An internal error occured while trying to obtain the list of all loaded configs on the remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server. This occured because Session.getConfigInstances() method threw an error.

OperatorResponse.p: Ensure that the tdisrvctl and remote IBM Security Verify Directory Integrator server versions match. Also look into the exception trace and server logs. Try again.

Message.MsgText: Already reached the end of argument list.

Message.MsgText:
The server hostname does not support deletion of tombstones.
Delete tombstone support is not available in pre-7.0 servers.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command tried deleting tombstones from a pre-7.0 server. Deletion of tombstones has been introduced from v7.0 onward.

OperatorResponse.p: Connect to a version 7.0 or later server for deleting tombstones.

Message.MsgText:
The usage for the tombsone deletion operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op deletetombstone -guid 'GUID # '
where:
-guid 'GUID # ' is the unique identifier for the tombstone to be deleted.
Note:
- GUID for a tombstone can be obtained by viewing a tombstone
Tombstone with guid GUID successfully deleted.
Temp configs cannot be run with password specified.

Explanation.p: The tdisrvctl command was invoked by specifying the -t (temp config) option in a combination with the -e (password) option, but temp configs cannot be started with a password.

OperatorResponse.p: Remove either the -t or -e option in order to successfully run the command.

Message.MsgText: It is mandatory to specify an AssemblyLine name. 'keyword' keyword is not allowed.

Explanation.p: Instead of passing the AssemblyLine name, the user asked for ALL AssemblyLines. This is not allowed. User must specify the AssemblyLine name.

OperatorResponse.p: Specify the explicit AssemblyLine name when invoking the tdisrvctl command. See tdisrvctl command usage.

Message.MsgText: Option 'option' is not allowed for operation 'option'.

Explanation.p: The user specified an option which is not supported for the specified operation.

OperatorResponse.p: See tdisrvctl command usage.

Explanation.p: The user specified debugging of components of an AssemblyLine that is not running on the server.

OperatorResponse.p: Check whether the AssemlyLine name is correct. Also check the tdisrvctl error logs for more information on the errors.

Message.MsgText: Could not set debug mode to component name component.

Explanation.p: The user specified a component that does not exist in the specified AssemblyLine.

OperatorResponse.p: Check whether the component name is correct. Also check the tdisrvctl error logs for more information on the errors.

Message.MsgText:
The usage for the debug operation is:
tdisrvctl [general_options] -op debug -c config -r assembly_line
[-alc al_component]
-on/off
where:
-c config config instance ID
-r assembly_line name of the AssemblyLine
-alc al_component name of the AssemblyLine component
-on flag to enable debug mode
-off flag to disable debug mode
Note:
- The -c and -r options are mandatory and require exactly one Config/AssemblyLine to be specified.
- If -alc option is not specified all components in the specified AssemblyLine will be affected.
Examples:
To view the Debug mode value of the components in the AssemblyLines of a specified Config
tdisrvctl -op report -c config
To enable the debug mode for all components in the running AssemblyLine al2
tdisrvctl -op debug -c config_name -r al2 -on
To disable the debug mode for specified components in the running AssemblyLine al3
tdisrvctl -op debug -c config_name -r al3 -alc fread,httpServer,myconn -off
